title: 1984 AHSME Problem 24
statement: If \(a\) and \(b\) are positive real numbers and each of the equations \[ \begin{aligned} x^2+ax+2b&=0,\\ x^2+2bx+a&=0 \end{aligned} \] has real roots, then the smallest possible value of \(a+b\) is

solutions.text:
The two discriminants give \(a^2\ge8b\) and \(b^2\ge a.\) Therefore \[ a^4\ge64b^2\ge64a. \] Since \(a\gt0,\) this yields \(a\ge4,\) and then \(b^2\ge a\ge4\) gives \(b\ge2.\) Thus \(a+b\ge6.\) Equality occurs at \(a=4,b=2,\) for which both discriminants are zero.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Require both quadratic discriminants to be nonnegative
Combine \(a^2\ge8b\) and \(b^2\ge a\) to bound \(a\) and \(b\)
